title: Scientific verification: N+1 query counting, SQLite locking (docs + experiment), and Prisma relation-loading semantics (docs + sandbox experiment)

problem.description: EXP-000010 (latest version v3, content of the v2 technical revision) claims: (1) the N+1 pattern runs a query count that grows with row count while a batched read runs a constant count — MEASURE FIRST with query logging; (2) SQLite 'database is locked' is a WRITE-transaction problem, separate from read-side N+1: in the rollback-journal model a write transaction holds RESERVED and takes the database lock at commit, blocking other WRITERS; WAL mode allows readers during a write; a missing busy timeout surfaces as immediate lock errors; (3) 'include = one JOIN' is NOT guaranteed — relation loading may compile to a JOIN or a constant number of batched queries depending on ORM version, provider and relation shape — the verifiable requirement is the constant query count, not a presumed SQL shape; (4) there is no depth threshold that alone mandates denormalization (the v1 rule was removed as unsupported). This run executes the record's own verification plan: V1 (SQLite docs) and V2 (locking experiment) on the user's machine, V4 (Prisma docs for the installed major version, 6.x) on the user's machine, and V0 (N+1 counting on real SQLite). V3 (Prisma runtime query counting) requires node — absent on the user's machine — and was executed in the Z.ai sandbox VM with Prisma 6.19.2 as supplementary evidence reported in the analysis.
problem.symptoms: list endpoints whose latency grows linearly with row count; SQLite 'database is locked' errors misdiagnosed as read-side N+1; assumed JOIN semantics for include; depth-threshold denormalization rules
problem.expectedBehavior: V0: the loop pattern executes exactly N+1 queries (501 at 500 parents) while the single JOIN executes 1, with the loop measurably slower. V2: with a short busy timeout a second writer gets 'database is locked' while another writer holds an open transaction; with a real busy timeout it succeeds after the holder commits; in WAL mode a reader proceeds during a pending write while a second writer is still blocked. V1: the official SQLite documentation documents the RESERVED/PENDING lock states, that there can only be one writer at a time in WAL, that readers do not block writers, and the busy-handler semantics. V4: the official Prisma v6 documentation documents the query-logging configuration (new PrismaClient({log:['query',...]}), event-based logging via $on) and defines the n+1 problem ('one additional query per result'), including the batching nuance that the dataloader 'does not currently batch findMany() queries'.
problem.actualBehavior: to be measured by real execution on the user's machine through the bridge (V0/V1/V2/V4) and in the Z.ai sandbox VM (V3, already executed: loop pattern 11->101 queries at 10->100 rows; include pattern a CONSTANT 2 queries — two batched SELECTs with an IN-list, NOT a single JOIN)
problem.facts: SQLite rollback-journal lock states are SHARED/RESERVED/PENDING/EXCLUSIVE (sqlite.org/lockingv3.html); WAL allows exactly one writer at a time while readers proceed concurrently (sqlite.org/wal.html); the busy handler sleeps for a specified time when a table is locked (sqlite.org/c3ref/busy_timeout.html); Prisma 6.19.2 + SQLite compiles findMany({include}) to two batched queries (parent SELECT + child SELECT with parentId IN (...)) as observed in the sandbox experiment with event-based query logging; the user's machine has sqlite3 3.46.1 (CLI) and python3 3.14.4 (bundled sqlite reported at runtime).
problem.assumptions: python3 stdlib sqlite3 on the user's machine behaves per the documented SQLite locking model; the sqlite.org and prisma.io pages fetched live are the authoritative current docs; the installed Prisma major version in the Z.ai sandbox (6.19.2, resolved from ^6.11.1) is representative of the v6 docs.
problem.environment: user's machine via the bridge extension: Linux, Python 3.14.4, sqlite3 CLI 3.46.1, no node; Z.ai sandbox VM for V3: bun + Prisma 6.19.2
problem.constraints: all experiments write only to mktemp temp dirs (nothing in the workspace); doc cases fetch only official sqlite.org and prisma.io pages and are flagged requiresNetwork; outputs below the 20KB truncation limit.

hypothesis.text: All four bridge cases pass their declared criteria on real execution: the N+1 count grows exactly linearly (501 vs 1 queries at 500 rows) with measurable latency difference; the rollback-journal lock error reproduces with a short busy timeout and clears with a real one; WAL lets readers proceed while writers still serialize; the SQLite documentation contains the lock-state definitions, one-writer and busy-handler statements; and the Prisma v6 documentation documents the logging configuration, the n+1 definition and the findMany batching nuance. Together with the sandbox V3 result (constant 2-query include, growing loop), this verifies the record's core claims: measure query count, not SQL shape; SQLite locking is a separate write-side problem; include semantics are version/provider-dependent.
hypothesis.supportingEvidence: VM-local dry-runs reproduce V0 (501 vs 1 queries, 31.2x slower loop) and V2 (lock error, busy-timeout success, WAL reader proceeds, WAL writer blocked) on Python 3.12.16/sqlite 3.53.1; the doc scripts verified all assertions against live fetches; the V3 sandbox experiment (Prisma 6.19.2) already produced its output, preserved at scripts/verifications/exp010/v3-prisma-experiment-output.txt.
hypothesis.contradictingEvidence: none observed in dry-runs; the Prisma SQLite connector doc page contains no locking/concurrency documentation (checked during design) — the locking claims are therefore verified against SQLite's own docs, which is the authoritative source.

strategy: Four bridge cases on the user's machine: V0 N+1 query counting on real SQLite (temp dir), V2 concurrent-writer locking experiment (rollback journal + WAL + busy timeout, threads, temp dir), V1 live SQLite documentation inspection (lockingv3, wal, busy_timeout), V4 live Prisma v6 documentation inspection (logging, query-optimization/N+1). V3 (Prisma runtime) executed in the Z.ai sandbox VM as supplementary labeled evidence. All cases critical; doc cases flagged requiresNetwork.
